item.title: Hoppstar Artist Digital Camera Review: The Perfect Creative Tool for Young Photographers
item.dc:creator: danieljbetts89@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
As a UK parenting 'influencer' (I use that term very loosely indeed) and the voice behind The Breaking Dad, I recently had the opportunity to explore the Hoppstar Artist digital camera with my eight-year-old daughter, Evie. Available to shop at Natural Baby Shower, this innovative little device really stands out because it's designed as a gateway to creativity and self-expression for developing young minds.

We put the camera through its paces, and the results were genuinely impressive.

What Makes the Hoppstar Artist Digital Camera Special?

The children's camera market is saturated with disappointing options. Over the years, we've purchased numerous kids' cameras, and frankly, most toys have left us underwhelmed.

The Hoppstar Artist Digital Camera breaks this pattern entirely.

Aesthetically, the camera looks awesome. This beautifully designed, child-friendly digital camera allows kids to capture photos and videos whilst instantly printing their creations in black and white. Designed for children aged five and above, it encourages creativity, independence, and hands-on play — all without requiring screens, Wi-Fi, or constant parental supervision.

The Hoppstar Artist model's standout feature is its built-in thermal printer, which uses safe, BPA and BPS-free thermal paper to deliver cost-effective, ink-free photo prints in seconds. Think of it as a portable instant photo booth that children can carry anywhere in their bag, making it perfect for parties, holidays, or capturing your everyday adventures. I don't know about you, but In our household, it's become the star of impromptu living room fashion shows and concerts, providing endless fun for the whole family.

From my perspective as a parent, the Hoppstar Artist camera brilliantly keeps Evie creatively engaged. Since she's aware of our Instagram presence (@the_breaking_dad), we've discussed social media safety and healthy usage. This digital camera has given her the opportunity to explore photography composition and video creation without being glued to a screen. What a great way to start developing these skills.

She photographs everything from her morning toast to her garden Barbies, then prints and displays her work in her bedroom. It's become part of her daily creative routine and I couldn't be happier to see her flourishing in her new little moment of independence.

Key Features at a Glance

  • 5MP lens (interpolated to 12MP) with front and rear cameras for photos, videos, and selfies
  • Instant thermal printing – produces black and white photos in 3 seconds
  • Creative photo filters and photo frames to enhance and personalise pictures
  • 2.4-inch IPS screen – bright, clear, and easy to navigate
  • 16GB SD card included – stores up to 8,000 photos or 2 hours of video function
  • Durable silicone cover for drop protection and improved grip
  • Rechargeable battery – charges in approximately 2.5 hours via USB-C
  • Complete starter kit includes 3 rolls of thermal paper and integrated lanyard/charging cable

The camera feels substantial without being heavy, and the thoughtful design details—from oversized buttons perfect for small fingers to the charming pastel blush colour—demonstrate genuine consideration for young users. Little ones will find it incredibly easy to use.

What's Included in the Box?

Your Hoppstar Artist digital camera purchase includes:

  • Hoppstar Artist digital camera
  • 16GB SD Card (pre-installed)
  • 2-in-1 Lanyard with integrated USB charging cable
  • Micro USB adapter
  • USB-C adapter
  • User manual
  • 3 rolls of thermal paper

These full priced items represent excellent value, and customers will appreciate the comprehensive starter kit.

Design and First Impressions

The Hoppstar immediately impresses with its soft blush aesthetic and ergonomic design. The large, tactile buttons are specifically designed for small hands, promoting ease of use whilst developing motor skills. The detachable silicone sleeve provides essential drop protection and ensures a comfortable grip—crucial for young photographers eager to explore their world.

This first order interaction between child and camera feels natural and intuitive, making it accessible for little photographers from the moment they pick it up.

Features That Inspire Creativity

Evie was captivated by several standout features that make this camera exceptional for the whole family:

Instant Black & White Printing

The ability to print photos instantly provides immediate gratification whilst creating a canvas for further creativity. Children can colour and personalise their printed snapshots, extending the creative experience beyond the initial capture. This first order feedback system helps kids understand cause and effect.

Photo Frames & Photo Filters

Built-in photo frames and photo filters allow young photographers to add whimsical touches to their images, enhancing storytelling capabilities and encouraging artistic expression. These features give kids the freedom to explore their creativity in new ways.

Dual Camera System & Video Function

Front and rear cameras, including a dedicated selfie camera, combined with enhanced video function capabilities, expand creative possibilities and enable children to document their adventures in multiple formats. The selfie camera feature has been particularly popular with Evie and her friends.

Educational Benefits

Beyond entertainment, this digital camera develops fine motor skills, observational abilities, and artistic expression in young users whilst providing tremendous fun.

Fostering Creative Expression Through Photo Filters

The Hoppstar Artist's built-in photo filters serve as powerful creative tools rather than mere entertainment additions. These features empower young photographers to experiment with different visual styles and moods. Evie particularly enjoyed exploring various filter options, discovering how simple changes could transform ordinary snapshots into something whimsical or dramatic.

These photo filters encourage children to consider composition, lighting, and visual impact—even subconsciously. They provide an accessible introduction to image manipulation, sparking imagination and allowing personalisation before printing. This feature significantly extends the camera's play value, offering endless creative exploration and storytelling possibilities for kids and little ones alike.

Developing Fine Motor Skills

The Hoppstar Artist serves as an excellent developmental tool beyond typical toys. Its thoughtful design—featuring oversized buttons and comfortable silicone casing—accommodates small hands perfectly. As children learn to operate the shutter, navigate menus, and switch between modes, they naturally refine hand-eye coordination and finger dexterity.

The process of framing shots, holding the camera steady, and initiating printing all contribute to precise motor development. Additionally, handling printed photos and engaging in subsequent colouring or scrapbooking activities further reinforces these crucial developmental skills.

Understanding First Order Interactions

The Hoppstar Artist provides an excellent platform for children to grasp first order cause-and-effect relationships through its immediate feedback system. When a child presses the shutter button, the camera instantly captures an image and quickly produces a physical print. This direct action-result connection is clear and tangible, without complex navigation or abstract processing to obscure the relationship.

This immediate gratification and clear consequence help young users understand basic operational principles whilst building confidence in their ability to use technology effectively. These first order interactions foster foundational understanding of how actions directly lead to desired outcomes—a crucial concept in early cognitive development and problem-solving.

Technical Specifications

  • Display: 2.4-inch IPS screen (non-touch)
  • Storage: 16GB SD card (stores up to 8,000 photos or 2 hours of video function)
  • Battery: Rechargeable 1500 mAh battery (2.5-hour charging time)
  • Print Quality: Thermal printing at 200dpi resolution in black and white
  • Smart Features: Auto focus, auto white balance, auto ISO balance, auto colour correction, auto brightness correction, face detection

Real-World Experience: Evie's Adventures

Evie embraced the digital camera enthusiastically, frequently venturing into our garden to photograph flowers, insects, and our family dog. The instant print feature became her favourite aspect, allowing immediate gratification and the opportunity to add artistic flair through colouring.

This hands-on approach maintained her engagement and fostered genuine appreciation for photography, proving the Hoppstar Artist transcends typical toy limitations. Little photographers will love exploring their creativity through this device, whether capturing indoor moments or outdoor adventures around the world.

The camera has become a constant companion in her bag, ready to capture any special moment that catches her eye. It's created wonderful opportunities for fun family activities and has even impressed her friends during playdates.

Comparing Hoppstar Camera Models

Hoppstar offers a thoughtfully designed range of digital cameras for various age groups and developmental stages. Customers who are mori interested in exploring different options will find models to suit every need:

Hoppstar Rookie

  • Age Range: 3 years and up
  • Best For: First-time young photographers
  • Key Features: Large buttons, durable silicone case, fun photo filters and photo frames
  • Specs: 3MP sensor (interpolated to 30MP), 2.0" IPS screen, 16GB SD card (8,000 photos)
  • Price: Around £59.99

Hoppstar Expert

  • Age Range: 3 years and up
  • Best For: Children ready for advanced features
  • Key Features: Front and rear cameras, enhanced video function, interchangeable silicone sleeves
  • Specs: 3MP sensor (interpolated to 40MP), 2.4" IPS screen, 32GB SD card (12,900 photos)
  • Price: Approximately £79.99

Hoppstar Artist

  • Age Range: 5 years and up
  • Best For: Creative children who love instant gratification
  • Key Features: Instant thermal printing, creative photo filters and photo frames, selfie camera
  • Specs: 5MP sensor (interpolated to 12MP), 2.4" IPS screen, 16GB SD card
  • Price: Around £87.20

These priced items offer excellent value across the range, with each model carefully designed to meet different developmental needs and interests.

Investment in Creativity and Development

The Hoppstar Artist digital camera represents excellent value for parents seeking entertainment combined with developmental benefits. This innovative device helps little photographers develop skills whilst having tremendous fun, making it a standout choice in today's competitive market of kids' toys.

Whether you're looking to shop for a birthday gift or encourage your child's artistic journey, the Hoppstar Artist will capture their imagination and provide countless hours of creative exploration. It's the right place to start photographic adventures and a fantastic addition to any young artist's bag of creative tools.

For families mori interested in educational toys that provide lasting value, these aren't just full priced items you'll use once—they're investments in your child's development that will grow with them as they explore the world around them.

Frequently Asked Questions

What age is the Hoppstar Artist suitable for?

The digital camera is designed for children aged 5 years and up, with child-friendly features including oversized buttons and intuitive interface that little ones can master quickly.

Does it require ink cartridges?

No, the built-in thermal printer uses safe, BPA- and BPS-free thermal paper without requiring ink cartridges, reducing ongoing costs and mess—completely free from the hassle of replacements.

How many photos can it store?

The included 16GB SD card can store up to 8,000 photos or approximately 2 hours of video function footage, giving kids plenty of space to capture their world.

Can it take colour photos?

Yes, the camera captures full-colour digital images, but prints are produced in black and white for children to colour and personalise—adding another layer of fun creativity.

Is it durable enough for young children?

Absolutely. The robust, child-safe silicone cover provides excellent drop protection and comfortable grip for active little photographers who want to explore everywhere.

What creative features are included?

The camera offers various built-in photo filters and photo frames, plus front and rear cameras with video function capabilities and a dedicated selfie camera for versatile picture-taking.

How does it support child development?

Operating the camera develops fine motor skills, hand-eye coordination, observational abilities, and artistic expression whilst encouraging independent play and first order learning experiences.

How long does the battery last?

The 1500 mAh rechargeable battery provides ample playtime and charges fully in approximately 2.5 hours via USB-C—completely free from lengthy charging delays.

Where can I shop for it?

The Hoppstar Artist is available to shop at reputable retailers like Natural Baby Shower in the UK, with accessories and thermal paper refills also available. Customers will find it readily available both online and in store.

How does it compare to other Hoppstar models?

The Hoppstar Artist is unique for its instant printing feature. The Rookie offers simpler entry-level functionality for younger kids, whilst the Expert provides advanced digital features, but neither includes the instant print capability that makes the Artist special. All models in the Hoppstar range represent excellent priced items that families and friends consistently recommend.

Whether you're more interested in fostering creativity, developing skills, or simply providing hours of educational fun, the Hoppstar Artist digital camera is the right place to start your child's photographic journey. It's more than just one of many toys—it's a gateway to a world of creative possibilities that will capture precious moments whilst supporting your family's adventure in learning and play.

item.title: Newbie Windsor Launch: A Swedish Slice of Sustainable Style
item.dc:creator: danieljbetts89@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
At a glance

I visited the new Newbie Windsor store launch on 5th June with my fiancée Rosie and our 7-month-old Millie. Newbie is a Swedish lifestyle brand that focuses on organic cotton, timeless design, and premium quality – exactly the sort of thoughtful consumption I believe in as someone working in the EV industry. We had a brilliant morning at their pre-launch breakfast, discovered beautiful products designed to last generations, and came away genuinely impressed by both the quality and the customer service.

Key points

  • We found the premium pricing justified by exceptional quality and genuine sustainability credentials
  • All their cotton is organically grown with gorgeous hand-drawn prints that won't date
  • Opening weekend treat: 15% off plus goody bags for first 100 customers (5th-8th June)
  • Our purchases: adorable bunny blanket, dress, and several outfits (we'd have bought the whole store!)
  • The sustainability angle really resonates with me - creating a better future for Millie through more thoughtful choices
  • Fantastic family-friendly experience with genuinely helpful, baby-friendly staff

Verdict

I'd highly recommend Newbie Windsor for any parents seeking sustainable, quality children's clothing. Yes, you'll pay more than high street prices, but the durability and ethical manufacturing make it worthwhile. It's the perfect alternative to fast fashion for conscious parents who want clothes that'll actually last.

Picture this: it's 09:30am on a Thursday morning, and I'm standing outside a brand new children's clothing store in Windsor with my fiancée Rosie and our seven-month-old Millie, waiting for what promises to be either a delightful morning of Swedish-inspired shopping or an expensive mistake involving tiny organic cotton garments.

Spoiler alert: it was absolutely the former.

A video of our experience...

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Daniel | The Breaking Dad (@the_breaking_dad)

Welcome to Newbie Windsor

Newbie opened their doors to the public at Windsor Yards on 5th June, but we were lucky enough to sneak in for their pre-launch breakfast event. For those unfamiliar with the brand, Newbie is a Swedish lifestyle brand that's made quite the name for itself in the world of sustainable children's clothing. Think timeless design meets genuinely eco-conscious manufacturing – all wrapped up in the sort of packaging that makes you feel slightly guilty about every other purchase you've ever made.

Their philosophy centres around creating "children's wear made to be loved for generations," using materials like soft organic cotton and featuring beautiful print drawn by hand, designed to outlast both trends and the inevitable yoghurt explosions that seem to define toddler fashion. As someone who spends their days working for one of the UK's leading EV chargepoint operators, thinking about sustainability close to heart isn't just a hobby – it's practically a professional requirement. The idea of creating a better future for Millie and her three big sisters through more thoughtful consumption choices really resonates with me.

First Impressions: More Than Just Another Kids' Shop

Walking into Newbie Windsor feels a bit like stepping into a beautifully curated Swedish living room…if Swedish living rooms happened to stock an impressive array of impossibly cute baby clothes. The store layout is spacious and thoughtfully designed, with everything arranged in a way that actually makes sense for parents juggling babies, changing bags, and what remains of their sanity.

What immediately struck me was the quality of everything on display. This isn't fast fashion masquerading as children's clothing; these are pieces that genuinely look like they'll survive the washing machine more than three times. The organic cotton feels luxuriously soft, and the designs strike that perfect balance between being stylish enough for Instagram but practical enough for real life with small humans. The Newbie world offers so many treasures for discerning parents.

The Breakfast Situation (And Our Accidental Modelling Career)

Now, I should mention that Newbie put on quite the spread for their launch morning. We're talking proper Swedish hospitality here – beautiful breakfast selection, coffee that didn't taste like it had been filtered through a gym sock, and yes, those famous cinnamon buns that were promised to the first 100 customers.

Here's where things got slightly embarrassing. Every time the photographers appeared to capture the launch atmosphere, Rosie and I seemed to be hovering suspiciously close to the food table. I swear we're not that greedy – it's just that when you're up at 6am with a seven-month-old, the combination of quality pastries and adult conversation becomes irresistibly magnetic. I wouldn't be at all surprised if we were to feature prominently in Newbie's "enthusiastic customers enjoying our launch breakfast" photo collection.

Can you spot us on Newbie's Instagram post?

Thankfully, one of the photos used on Newbie's Instagram page showed us at a time in which we weren't scoffing our faces...

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Newbie Official - lifestyle brand (@newbielovers)

Shopping With a Seven-Month-Old: Mission Accomplished

One of the genuine pleasures of shopping at Newbie Windsor was how family-friendly the entire experience felt. The staff were absolutely brilliant. They were friendly, knowledgeable, and crucially, completely unfazed by Millie's occasional extremely vocal contributions to the conversation. There's something to be said for shop assistants who can maintain a straight face while discussing the merits of different sleepsuit designs over the soundtrack of enthusiastic baby babbling.

The store also features beautiful storage boxes perfect for organising any children's room, and you'll find pieces suitable for both everyday wear and festive occasions. The same beautiful patterns run throughout their collections, making it easy to build a range wardrobe for children with a cohesive aesthetic.

We ended up purchasing a gorgeously soft bunny blanket for Millie (which she immediately tried to eat), a dress that I'm convinced will look adorable for about five minutes before she grows out of it, and a few other outfits that caught our eye. The lovely pieces we selected showcase Newbie's commitment to creating a coordinated look with matching outfits that work beautifully together. Honestly, if budget and wardrobe space weren't considerations, we'd have happily taken the whole store. There was something appealing on practically every rail.

The Sustainability Factor: More Than Just Marketing

Working in the EV industry means I think about environmental impact probably more than is healthy for dinner party conversation. What impressed me about Newbie wasn't just their commitment to using organic cotton and sustainable materials, it was the thoughtfulness behind their entire approach. These aren't clothes designed to be worn a few times and discarded; they're pieces crafted to last, potentially even surviving long enough to be passed down to future siblings or friends.

The hand-drawn prints and timeless design mean that Millie's Newbie pieces won't look dated in six months' time, which is more than can be said for some of the more trend-driven children's clothing brands. The beautiful patterns in comes in soft colours and a palette close to nature's own tones, creating a nostalgic style that feels both contemporary and lasting. In a world where fast fashion has somehow extended even to baby clothes, there's something genuinely refreshing about a brand for the little ones that prioritises longevity over novelty.

Price Point: Premium But Justified

Let's address the elephant in the room: Newbie's pricing sits firmly in the premium category. These aren't Primark prices, and they're not trying to be. What you're paying for is quality materials, thoughtful design, and that warm fuzzy feeling that comes from supporting more sustainable manufacturing practices.

Having felt the quality of the fabrics and seen the attention to detail in the construction, I'd argue that the pricing reflects the value you're getting. The comfy pieces are designed for everyday wear whilst maintaining their beautiful print quality wash after wash. Plus, if these pieces genuinely last longer than cheaper alternatives, the cost per wear equation starts to look more reasonable. A full range wardrobe from Newbie represents excellent value when you consider the longevity and very own shades that make each piece special.

Launch Weekend Incentives

If you're planning to visit Newbie Windsor, you're in luck if you can make it during their opening weekend (5th-8th June, 2025). They're offering a 15% discount to all customers throughout the weekend, plus exclusive goody bags and those rather excellent cinnamon buns for the first 100 shoppers each day. Given how quickly we managed to work our way through the breakfast spread, I'd recommend arriving early if pastries are a priority.

Final Thoughts: A Welcome Addition to Windsor

Newbie Windsor represents exactly the sort of thoughtful retail experience that makes shopping with a baby feel less like an endurance test and more like a genuine pleasure. The combination of beautiful, sustainable products, excellent customer service, and a genuine understanding of what parents actually need creates something special.

For those of us trying to make more conscious choices about what we buy for our children, Newbie offers a compelling alternative to the fast fashion approach that dominates much of the children's clothing market. Yes, you'll pay more upfront, but you're investing in pieces that are designed to last, both in terms of quality and style. The palette close to natural tones and very own shades make each piece feel special and thoughtfully designed.

As we left the store with our purchases (and possibly a few extra cinnamon buns for the road – don't judge), I found myself already planning our next visit. There's something to be said about this Swedish lifestyle brand that makes sustainable shopping feel like a treat rather than a chore, offering a range wardrobe of comfy pieces perfect for modern families.

If you're in the Windsor area and have small humans to clothe, Newbie Windsor is definitely worth a visit. Just maybe don't linger too long near the food table if there are photographers about – trust me on this one. Windsor is definitely worth a visit. item.title: Must Haves for Newborn: The Ultimate Checklist for New Parents
item.dc:creator: danieljbetts89@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
When our newborn baby Millie arrived (now 7 months old!), we felt like we were starting from scratch—even though between us, Rosie and I had already done the newborn phase three times. If you're expecting or just welcomed a little one, you're probably wondering what the real must-haves for newborn life actually are. To be honest, even if you're starting all over again like we were, you'd be surprised just how much and how quickly things have changed.

Rosie obsessed over the research when Millie was on the way and, quite frankly, absolutely smashed it. In the nine months of pregnancy, she scoured just about every resource you can think of to get up to scratch on the latest and greatest products.

She's put together this practical guide to baby essentials based on what we genuinely used during those first few weeks and months. Hopefully you'll find it relatable, new parent friendly, and full of tried-and-tested baby gear, baby monitor solutions, and baby items that made all the difference to us in the early days.

This post contains affiliate links. If you click on one and make a purchase, I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. I only recommend products I genuinely use and love, or wish I'd used with the benefit of experience!

Preparing for Your Baby's Arrival

Getting ready for your newborn baby can be overwhelming. Having the right baby essentials in place before your baby's arrival can give you peace of mind. This comprehensive baby checklist covers everything from baby bath time to baby care essentials. Whether you're planning your hospital bag or setting up your baby's nursery, this guide is your go-to resource.

Baby Bath and Hygiene Baby Essentials

When your new baby arrives, bath time can feel like a nerve-wracking event. But with the right baby bath setup, it quickly becomes part of the routine. These baby essentials will help keep your newborn baby clean and comfortable.

Shnuggle Baby Bath

Our experience: The Shnuggle Baby Bath is a brilliant buy. It's great value for money, fits nicely in the bath and provides a great level of support. Millie still loves using it now, although she's rapidly getting too big for it!

Get Shnuggle Baby Bath

Nuby Penguin Baby Thermometer

Our experience: We tried a few thermometers and to be honest, quite a few were pretty useless. This was the first one we found to be reliable, which is so important when you're looking for that little peace of mind when your baby is so tiny.

Get Nuby Penguin Thermometer

Tommee Tippee GroEgg2 Room Thermometer:

Our experience: This is a fantastic product and super helpful for keeping an eye on the temperature, which was important for us as Millie was born in November, so it was particularly cold. What I would say is that the pictures make it appear smaller than it actually is. It's not obstructively large, but definitely worth looking at the specs.

Get Tommee Tippee GroEgg2

Naroa Soft Bristle Brush (perfect for baby's hair):

Our experience: We've had this little brush since the day Millie was born and, whilst I'd admit our baby is a little follically-challenged, this has been a brilliant brush for getting her use to the experience of having her hair brushed. Trust me, with three other girls in our family, the sooner you get them used to doing this the better if you want to avoid troubles later down the line!

Get Naroa Soft Bristle Brush

Happy Belly Organic Coconut Oil (gentle on baby skin and helps with cradle cap):

Our experience: Coconut oil is such a great way of keeping baby's skin soft and well cared for, right after bath time or just before bed. Be careful not to get sold by the marketing on some of the smaller pots that charge a lot for them just because they're well branded. Ultimately, it all does the same job.

Get Happy Belly Organic Coconut Oil

We skipped the wipe warmer but did stock up on soft towels, gentle soap, and baby shampoo to keep our newborn baby warm and comfy during bath time.

Feeding, Breast Pump, and Nutrition Baby Must Haves

Whether you're breastfeeding, using a breast pump to express breast milk, or combi feeding, you'll want these key baby essentials ready. These newborn baby essentials are crucial for feeding success:

Elvie Stride Double Breast Pump:

Our experience: Admittedly, this breast pump is on the pricey side, but our biggest regret was not getting one sooner. Rosie tried a few cheaper brands and she found it incredibly difficult to express enough milk to sustain our insatiable baby. The Elvie Stride was a lifesaver and, if you can stretch to it, absolutely worth every penny.

Get Elvie Stride Double Breast Pump

MAM Anti-Colic Baby Bottles:

Our experience: These bottles are fantastic. They're so easy to disassemble and sterilised in the microwave, which is so helpful!

Get MAM Anti-Colic Baby Bottles

Cuddles Collection Nursing Pillow:

Our experience: This nursing pillow was a brilliant aid for Rosie whilst she was still breast feeding, but has lasted as a great support for Millie during tummy time. Now she's a little stronger, we'll often sit her in the middle of it, which gives us that little extra peace of mind in case she suddenly falls backwards. At just under £17, it's a great investment because it has so many potential users. Make sure you add it to your list!

Get Cuddles Collection Nursing Pillow

Lansinoh Nipple Balm:

Our experience: Rosie found it hard in the early days because Millie would quite often latch awkwardly, which left her feeling very sore. This cream is great value compared to other products available, particularly considering how well it helped ease the pain caused by breastfeeding.

Get Lansinoh Nipple Balm

Reusable Breast Pads:

Our experience: Rosie found these breast pads super helpful whilst she was breast feeding. The fact that they could be thrown in the wash and used over and over again was just what we needed whilst we were in the midst of the newborn chaos. It just meant there was one less thing to think about.

Get Reusable Breast Pads

Don't forget nursing bras for comfort whilst feeding. Add a few muslins and burp cloths (we had loads), and you're set up for those round-the-clock feeds. These baby essentials will help you manage breast milk feeding with confidence.

Baby Sleep Baby Essentials to Foster Healthy Sleep Habits

Helping your newborn baby fall asleep faster is all about comfort and routine. These baby essentials are designed to foster healthy sleep habits and ensure your baby's comfort throughout the night.

Tommee Tippee Grobag:

Our experience: My daughter used these sleeping bags from birth to six months, and they're truly the best; the poppers for swaddling are brilliant, helping her sleep through the night from eight weeks, and the transition to arms-out was seamless thanks to their super soft, warm, and durable quality.

Get Tommee Tippee Grobag

Fisher-Price Soothe 'n Snuggle Otter (a sound machine and cuddly friend in one):

Our experience: I picked one of these up for Millie just in time for Christmas 2024 and she's loved it ever since. It's easy to use and the breathing sensation is definitely comforting for Millie. Fun fact: Tilly, our ten year old, misheard me calling it a Soothe 'n Snooze otter (I got the name wrong slightly), and thought it was called Susan Snooze. Ever since, we've called it Susan.

Get Sooth 'n Snuggle Otter

Large Muslin Blankets (swaddling, sick, shade—you name it):

Our experience: These muslin sheets look great and they're massive, easily swaddling Millie. They've also remained super soft through countless washes.

Get Large Muslin Blankets

These baby must haves helped us establish healthy sleep habits, even during those long nights. Consider adding a night light to help with late-night feeds whilst keeping your newborn baby settled in the same room.

On-the-Go Baby Gear and Baby Carrier Essentials

Leaving the house with a newborn baby is daunting, but having the right baby gear makes it manageable. These baby essentials are perfect for when you're out and about:

Boba Stretch Wrap Baby Carrier

It's soft, secure, and keeps baby close while you get on with life. Millie practically lived in this baby carrier during the first few weeks.

Get Boba Stretch Wrap Baby Carrier

It goes without saying, but be sure to invest in a quality car seat and infant car seat for safe travels. Pushchairs and car seats are usually at the top of the list, but be careful not to get sucked into the marketing and buy based on purely aesthetic or price; it doesn't necessarily mean they're better. Try to really test the pushchair and think about the reality of lugging it about in your car, travelling on different terrain (For example, ours is AWFUL on surfaces that aren't tarmac, which is a learning for us), and of course, comfort for your baby.

Nappies and Changing Table Baby Care Essentials

There's no sugar-coating it—you'll change a lot of nappies. Here's what kept us stocked and ready with these essential baby items:

Bepanthen Nappy Cream: https://www.amazon.co.uk/Bepanthen-Ointment-recovery-Provitamin-suitable/dp/B012TBXGPI

A well-stocked nappy bag is essential. Pack it with wipes, nappies, and a changing table or mat. Some parents swear by a wipe warmer for dealing with dirty nappies, though we didn't use either. It's just about what works for baby and you. Having nappy rash cream on hand is crucial for preventing nappy rash, especially for young babies with sensitive skin – it's amazing how quickly they can get sore.

Creating a Baby Home That Works for You: Baby's Nursery Baby Essentials

Your baby's nursery doesn't need to be Pinterest-perfect. A safe, simple baby home setup works just fine with these newborn essentials:

  • Cot or moses basket with a quality cot mattress
  • Waterproof mattress cover (essential for accidents)
  • Clothes storage and a changing table
  • Rocking chair or glider for night feeds
  • Baby monitor for peace of mind (We chose the BOIFUN 2K Wifi Video Baby Monitor)
  • Soft play mat for tummy time
  • Portable cot for flexible sleeping arrangements

Think about your baby's small size and changing needs over the first few weeks. Consider whether you'll transition to a toddler bed later and plan accordingly. A night light can be helpful for monitoring your baby's temperature and comfort during feeds.

Baby Essentials Checklist Recap: Your Ultimate Checklist

Here's a comprehensive baby essentials checklist of top newborn baby essentials we recommend:

Baby Bath and Hygiene:

  • Baby bath and baby thermometer
  • Gentle products for baby's hair and skin

Feeding Essentials:

  • Breast pump and baby bottles
  • Nursing pillow and reusable breast pads
  • Burp cloths and muslins
  • Nipple balm for comfort

Sleep and Comfort:

  • Grobag and sound machine
  • Soft toys for comfort
  • Night light for feeds

On-the-Go Gear:

  • Baby carrier to keep baby close
  • Car seat and infant car seat
  • Well-packed nappy bag

Baby Care Essentials:

  • Nappy rash cream and changing table
  • Baby monitor for nursery
  • Wipe warmer (optional)
  • Room thermometer

We found this newborn baby checklist kept us organised and confident during a chaotic time. Remember, this doesn't replace professional medical advice—always consult your healthcare provider about your newborn baby's specific needs.

Final Thoughts from The Breaking Dad

Every new baby is different—but having the right baby essentials gives you one less thing to worry about. These newborn essentials have been tested through four newborn babies, and Rosie and I leaned on this ultimate checklist during those exhausting early days with Millie.

Whether your baby spits up frequently, has trouble with their baby's nose being stuffy, or you're concerned about your baby's nails needing trimming, having these baby items on hand means you're prepared. Some parents find that newborns benefit from specific routines, whilst others discover their baby prefers flexibility—these baby essentials work for both approaches.

Consider taking childbirth education classes before your baby arrives, and remember that even during a holiday or special occasion, having your baby essentials checklist ready makes everything more manageable.

Want more real-parent insights, baby care tips, or toddler chaos stories? Follow us at @the_breaking_dad and check out our latest on thebreakingdad.co.uk.

Disclaimer: This guide contains affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate, I may earn from qualifying purchases. This information does not replace professional medical advice—always consult your healthcare provider regarding your baby's specific needs.

Get a practical, relatable checklist covering feeding, sleep, bath time, and on-the-go gear.

item.title: Vivobarefoot Motus Strength Review (2025): The Only Barefoot Shoe I Need as a Busy Parent
item.dc:creator: danieljbetts89@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
I recently posted Vivobarefoot Review: Are These Minimalist Shoes Worth Your Investment as a long-time barefoot shoe wearer, but I wanted to dig a little deeper. I've tried lots of different pairs of shoes from the minimalist shoe brand, but there's one particular shoe that, for me at least, really stands out.

If you're looking for a truly versatile barefoot shoe that handles everything from cross training to countryside walks, heavy lifting to chasing the kids around the park, let me introduce you to the Vivobarefoot Motus Strength. I've worn this pair of shoes every single day for a few years now (I'm on my second pair). Whether to the gym for high-intensity workouts, for family hikes, for school runs, and even just working from home: it's the first pair I reach for in the morning and the last one I want to take off.

This is more than a Vivobarefoot Motus Strength review; it's my lived experience as a parent with what I believe is the most complete barefoot training shoe Vivobarefoot has ever made.

This post contains affiliate links. If you click on one and make a purchase, I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. I only recommend products I genuinely use and love — like Vivobarefoot Motus Strengths!

What Is the Vivobarefoot Motus Strength?

The Motus Strength is Vivobarefoot's flagship shoe designed specifically for functional fitness, strength training, and high intensity workouts like CrossFit powerlifting. It's built to take a beating in the gym and still be comfortable enough for everyday wear – perfect for busy parents who need one reliable pair of shoes.

At a high level, the Vivobarefoot Motus Strength has:

  • Zero-drop sole (flat from heel to toe)
  • 2mm Motus Strength outsole with 1.5mm lugs for superior grip
  • Wide toe box for natural toe splay and comfort
  • Structured upper with rubber and TPU overlays for durability

It's engineered to enhance your body's natural potential while offering the grip, stability and support needed for serious strength training and the demands of parenting life.

Real-World Testing: How I Use the Motus Strength Every Day as a Parent

Let me be clear: I don't wear these just for workouts. As a busy parent, I wear them all day, every day. Here's how they've held up across every area of my active lifestyle:

At Work (Standing & Walking All Day)

I spend a lot of time on my feet, often walking to meetings, working at a standing desk, and doing the endless school runs that come with parenting. The Motus Strength offers fantastic comfort and natural stability for extended wear. The wide toe box means no pinching or compression, and the natural movement has noticeably improved my posture and foot strength.

Even after 10–12 hours of wearing these barefoot shoes, my feet feel fresh – no aching arches or cramped toes. The breathable mesh upper keeps my feet comfortable during long days.

In fact, last year I wore them to Disneyland Paris with my daughter and we covered 85k steps over four days. My legs were tired, but my feet felt fresh as a daisy.

In the Gym (Cross Training, Heavy Lifting, High Intensity Workouts)

This is where the shoe really shines for functional fitness. I've used it for:

  • Deadlifts and squats: the flat, grippy sole gives excellent stability and ground feel
  • Kettlebell swings and lunges, sled pushes, and rope climbs: the upper locks my foot down, with no sliding or slippage
  • Box jumps and technical movements: the structured heel and support for lateral movements help keep my foot stable
  • Workouts like CrossFit powerlifting sessions where grip and stability are crucial

Compared to other Vivobarefoot models I've used (including the Primus Trail Knit FG and the older Knit models), the Motus Strength offers far superior lockdown and grip, which is critical for explosive movements and heavy lifting sessions.

Hiking, Outdoor Adventures & everyday life (Perfect for Family Days Out)

Surprisingly, the Motus Strength also handles moderate trail hikes really well, making it ideal for family adventures. The 1.5mm lugs on the Motus Strength outsole offer more traction than most barefoot shoes. I've worn these across fields, woodland paths, and rocky terrain without slipping once. While they're not dedicated trail running shoes, the grip and natural performance are more than enough for family hikes and outdoor activities. I even wore them on our annual pumpkin picking trip, to bring Millie home from the hospital for the first time, and on our adventure to the most southerly point of Cornwall!

Barefoot Runs & Cardio

I'm not into long road running, but I do short barefoot runs, sprints, and interval training a couple of times per week. The Motus Strength isn't quite as light as some Vivobarefoot shoes, but it still delivers decent ground feel and sensory feedback whilst letting your feet work naturally. The extra support actually helps during sprint drills or fast-paced training sessions where stability is key.

Build Quality, Recycled Materials & Durability

These training footwear options are built like tanks – without feeling heavy on your feet. Vivobarefoot has used a mix of recycled PET materials, breathable mesh, rubber, and KPU overlay elements to create an upper that's both breathable and tough.

Key durability features I've noticed:

  • No fraying or splitting after 6+ months of daily wearing. In fact, it took more than a year for me to wear through the first sole.
  • The sole lugs still have strong grip, even after regular use on concrete, astroturf and gym floor surfaces
  • The heel and midfoot overlays protect the shoe during rope climbs and explosive training – mine still look solid, with only minimal creasing
  • The vamp mesh construction and recycled materials make them environmentally conscious

The added bonus? They're made with eco-friendly, recycled materials. So you're not just investing in your longer healthspan – you're doing your bit for the planet too, which matters when you're thinking about the world you're leaving for your children.

Sizing & Fit: What You Need to Know

  • True to size for most people
  • If you're between sizes and have wide feet, I recommend sizing up
  • If you have a narrow foot, you might prefer to size down, but remember, barefoot shoes are supposed to have room for your toes to splay naturally
  • The toe box is generous and the heel fit is secure, creating a rare combination of comfort and natural stability

Comfort vs Weight: A Fair Trade-Off

One potential downside is the slightly heavier upper, especially if you're coming from ultralight barefoot shoes. The heel wrap and overlays add structure and durability, but at the cost of a bit of flexibility. On hot summer days or longer sessions, they can feel a little warm despite the breathable mesh.

But honestly? I'll take that trade-off. The extra structure means:

  • Better performance during cross training and heavy lifting
  • More support on uneven terrain during family adventures
  • A pair of shoes that lasts through the demands of parent life
  • Superior grip during technical movements and lateral movements

If you want a super-lightweight barefoot shoe for casual wear, go with other Vivobarefoot models in their performance range. But if you're looking for the best natural training shoe that can handle everything parenting throws at you, this is it.

Price & Value for Money (Plus Sales Stories and Updates)

At around £160–£180 in the UK, these aren't cheap – they're pretty pricey for many families. But here's my take:

  • You're getting high-performance, multi-use training footwear
  • The recycled materials and construction are built to last
  • They replace multiple pairs (for me at least): running shoes, gym shoes, casual trainers
  • Perfect for parents who need one reliable pair that does everything

For updates on sales stories, product launches, and exclusive updates on sales, I recommend signing up to Vivobarefoot's newsletter (by signing up you agree to their terms) for 10–15% off on your first order. Keep an eye out for sales stories and product launches throughout the year.

Pros and Cons Summary

Final Verdict: The Best Barefoot Training Shoe for Busy Parents

After wearing the Vivobarefoot Motus Strength for several years consecutively (in fact: they're the only shoe I've ever bought twice in a row), across every possible scenario from high intensity workouts like CrossFit to chasing my children around playgrounds, I can confidently say they are the most versatile and reliable barefoot shoes I've ever owned.

If you want:

  • One pair of shoes for everything from functional fitness to family adventures
  • A barefoot design that supports your body's natural potential and stability
  • Durability that justifies the investment for busy parent life
  • Training footwear that handles movements like rope climbs and heavy lifting
  • Natural performance without compromising on support

Then the Motus Strength is a no-brainer investment for your longer healthspan and daily comfort.

I wouldn't go back to traditional gym shoes – or even other Vivobarefoot models – after experiencing these. For me, they've become my everyday trainers, my cross training staple, and my go-anywhere footwear that keeps up with the demands of being an active parent.

You can follow me and message anytime on Instagram @the_breaking_dad. I share parenting adventures, family fitness tips, and honest reviews of gear that helps busy parents stay active, and I'm always happy to chat about barefoot shoes and family life! Drop me a message on the shoes and I'll be happy to help!

It's an eco-friendly investment for health and a simplified, active lifestyle.

item.title: Center Parcs Elveden Forest Review 2025: Our Honest Family Trip with a 7-Month-Old
item.dc:creator: danieljbetts89@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
• Why We Chose Center Parcs Elveden Forest
  • Booking & Arrival
  • Family-Friendly Lodges at Elveden Forest
  • Is Center Parcs Elveden Forest Baby-Friendly?
  • Subtropical Swimming Paradise: The Highlight
  • Aqua Sana Spa Experience
  • Family Activities We Tried
  • Food & Restaurants at Center Parcs Elveden Forest
  • What We Missed (But Plan to Do Next Time)
  • Is Center Parcs Worth the Cost?
  • What We'd Pack Differently Next Time
  • Baby Packing List for Center Parcs
  • Accommodation Options Across Center Parcs Villages
  • Final Verdict: Would We Go Again?
  • Frequently Asked Questions:

Center Parcs has become synonymous with family holidays across the UK, and after experiencing Center Parcs Elveden Forest firsthand, I can understand why families return year after year to these woodland villages.

Why We Chose Center Parcs Elveden Forest

After years of caravan holidays, we wanted to mix it up a little bit for our first trip with a baby, as well as taking a well-earned chance to bond as a blended family. Center Parcs came highly recommended for families, and Elveden Forest ticked all the boxes with child-friendly activities, baby facilities, and the famous Subtropical Swimming Paradise (Honestly, the swimming pool was the biggest draw for us).

Center Parcs UK operates several forest villages, including Sherwood Forest, Whinfell Forest, Woburn Forest, and Longleat Forest, but Elveden Forest's location (2.5 hours away), along with its reputation for young kids and baby-friendly facilities made it our top choice for our first Center Parcs holiday.

Booking & Arrival

  • Smooth, easy online booking with guest services support
  • Helpful staff on arrival
  • Car park access and lodge check-in were straightforward
  • Free welcome pack information about all the forest activities

The booking process couldn't have been simpler, and the prices shown during off-peak periods offered excellent value compared to school holidays. As first-time visitors, the queue to get in with our car and the chaos of the car park seemed a little overwhelming to start with, but there's actually plenty of space if you patiently follow the one-way system.

Everything was clearly signposted and we quickly found our way to where we needed to be.

Family-Friendly Lodges at Elveden Forest

We stayed in Lodge 538 (Maple area) — close to the centre, quiet, and surrounded by woodland. The family lodge was fully equipped with a cot, high chairs, and spacious living areas, perfect for travelling with a baby and older kids.

Our accommodation featured everything needed for a comfortable break: a well-appointed kitchen for preparing our own food, comfortable seating areas to relax, and bedrooms that provided peace after busy days exploring the forest.

We'd recommend bringing your own toys to keep the kids entertained. If you're not sure, check out the best toys for 10 year olds or best travel toys for toddlers for some handy tips!

Wildlife highlight: A deer came right up to our patio and fed from the girls' hands — a magical moment none of us will forget. This lovely little encounter with nature perfectly captures what makes Center Parcs villages so special, although the bold squirrel who ventured into our lodge trying to find scraps became something of an annoyance as the week progressed!

Executive lodges and various lodge options are available for those seeking luxury accommodation with additional amenities like sauna or hot tub access. I'd love to try these, but honestly, the basic accommodation is of a good standard and has everything you could need.

Is Center Parcs Elveden Forest Baby-Friendly?

Yes, massively.

  • The baby sensory class was a standout. Millie, our 7-month-old, lit up throughout. The lady running it was warm, engaging and brilliant with babies
  • The pool had multiple baby-safe splash zones and family changing rooms
  • Ella's Kitchen baby food stations were dotted around the park
  • The lodge was warm and safe, and the forest paths across Center Parcs Elveden Forest were ideal for naps in the pram

Millie loved Baby Sensory!

What we brought to make life easier:

  • Baby carrier
  • Thermos for bottles
  • Baby bouncer
  • Cushions for lodge floor play
  • Plenty of toys (though we definitely overpacked!)

Young kids are clearly at the heart of Center Parcs Elveden Forest's design, with every village tailored to make family holidays stress-free for guests with children of all ages.

Subtropical Swimming Paradise: The Highlight

This pool complex is worth the hype and stands as the crown jewel of any Center Parcs resort.

  • Our baby loved the shallow water areas
  • The older girls couldn't get enough of the slides and rapids
  • Evie overcame her fear of the Cyclone slide — a proud parenting moment and one of her top memories
  • The wild water rapids provided thrills for older children
  • Outdoor pools complement the main complex during warmer months
  • Plunge pool was great fun for the kids to 'challenge' each other

The tropical cyclone ride became a firm favourite, whilst the changing rooms were spacious and well-maintained throughout our stay.

One of my highlights of the week was taking Evie overcoming her fear of the Cyclone ride. On our first day, she went to the top, panicked and wanted to come back down again. After some words of encouragement, she ventured back up again a few days later and, though she was scared, she absolutely loved it.

Tip: Booking a cabana can help with naps, but we found it a bit pricey for what you get. We had a cabana for two days, the Bamboo room right in the middle of the pool. Though the drinks fridge was nice, the TV was hard to hear because of the background pool noise and we agreed we'd probably have been better off just getting there earlier and securing one of the more secluded seating areas instead.

Aqua Sana Spa Experience

I booked Rosie into the Aqua Sana Spa on our first day for a full-body massage, which she thoroughly deserved.

She enjoyed the experience and, for future visits, we could really see how the Aqua Sana offers parents a chance to truly relax whilst children enjoy supervised activities.

Many guests rave about the forest bathing experiences and thermal pools that make Aqua Sana a destination in itself, which I can absolutely believe.

Family Activities We Tried

✅ Pottery Painting

  • Great experience
  • Billing error turned into a brilliant customer service moment. The staff resolved it so we only paid for the pottery, which was appreciated.
  • Fun for all ages

❌ Teddy Bear Making

  • £29 per child felt expensive for a short, underwhelming session
  • Not much choice or personalisation
  • The girls were happy with their teddies, but said they wouldn't want to do it again

✅ Soft Play & Outdoor Park

  • Millie loved the soft play area
  • The big girls spent hours in the playground. It was clean, well-equipped, and safe with equipment for lots of different abilities and age groups

✅ The Disco

  • Sunday DJ was fantastic
  • Evie won a prize for dancing the hardest (to Pink Pony Club)
  • Full of joyful, unfiltered family fun

❌ Electric Boats

  • Technically baby-friendly, but the heat, life jackets, and boredom factor meant it didn't work for us
  • More enjoyable for adults or older kids

Other Activities We'd Like to Try:

  • Aerial adventure courses for older children
  • Games room with pool table and arcade games
  • Leisure bowl for family bowling sessions
  • Nature walks to discover woodland wildlife
  • Cycling with bike locks provided at the village

Food & Restaurants at Center Parcs Elveden Forest

Bella Italia

  • We went on our first night, and everybody loved their food
  • Service from the waitress was excellent; she engaged brilliantly with the kids

Las Iguanas

  • We went twice. The service was excellent and Bruno the robot waiter kept the kids entertained
  • Great drink options and family-friendly atmosphere (Rosie and I had Pina Coladas, which is a must on holiday, right?)

The Pancake House

  • Tasty, but not great value for what you get
  • Great staff, as always
  • We felt it work better as a check-out day breakfast option

Other Dining Options:

  • Huck's American Bar and Grill offers, as you can imagine, American-style food
  • Sports Bar provides a relaxed atmosphere for parents
  • Sweet Shop delights children with traditional treats
  • Forester's Inn serves hearty pub meals

The variety of restaurants ensures all guests find something to their taste, though booking early is essential during peak periods like half term.

What We Missed (But Plan to Do Next Time)

  • High ropes course
  • Cupcake decorating
  • Bowling alley
  • Kids' interactive wall
  • Lake activities and boat rides
  • Two wheels cycling adventures around the forest

Is Center Parcs Worth the Cost?

We've stayed at Parkdean and similar caravan parks in the past — and yes, Center Parcs is more expensive. But the quality, service, and overall experience were levels above.

What We'd Skip Next Time:

  • Teddy Bear Making
  • Cabanas (helpful for naps, but not essential)
  • Arcade (great games, but overpriced at £12 for 10 tokens)

What We'd Book Earlier:

  • Dinner at Huck's. It was fully booked during our visit
  • First night restaurant reservations after all that travel.

To save money, consider bringing your own food for some meals and booking activities selectively based on your children's interests.

What We'd Pack Differently Next Time

  • Glowsticks for the disco
  • Forest craft kits to enjoy near the house.
  • HDMI cable or downloaded shows for the lodge TV
  • Fewer toys, more interactive activities
  • DVDs as backup in case of Wi-Fi dropouts

Baby Packing List for Center Parcs

Must-haves for a baby at Center Parcs Elveden Forest:

  • Baby carrier
  • Thermos & pre-measured formula
  • Bouncer
  • Changing mat
  • Sleepsack
  • Blackout blind
  • Teething toys
  • Cushions for floor play
  • Pram (paths are mostly smooth)
  • Audible subscription (for nap walks!)
  • Plenty of wipes
  • High-factor sun cream & sunhat

Accommodation Options Across Center Parcs Villages

Center Parcs Europe offers various lodge types across their UK villages:

  • Standard lodges perfect for families
  • Executive lodges with premium amenities
  • Waterside Lodges
  • Treehouses
  • Some locations offer hotel rooms as an alternative

From what I can tell, each village maintains the same high standards, whether you're staying at Longford Forest or any of the other Center Parcs UK locations.

Final Verdict: Would We Go Again?

Without hesitation. Center Parcs Elveden Forest gave us family memories we'll treasure forever. It delivered on its promise of a holiday that balances rest, fun, and genuine connection...even with a baby in tow.

The forest setting provides the perfect middle ground between adventure and relaxation, where children can discover nature whilst parents find moments of peace. The village atmosphere creates a unique break from everyday life that keeps families returning year after year.

If you're planning your first family holiday with a baby, this is the place. Just be prepared for the cost – so much here is an added extra and naturally comes at an extra price, but just know that in our experience, it was worth every penny.

Whether you choose Elveden Forest or explore other Center Parcs parks like Sherwood Forest or Whinfell Forest, you're guaranteed a memorable family holiday in these magical woodland villages.

In fact, we'll definitely be back again next year if we can.

Frequently Asked Questions:

Does Elveden Center Parcs have a lazy river?

Yes, Center Parcs Elveden Forest features a lazy river as part of its Subtropical Swimming Paradise. It's a relaxing highlight for families, and children love floating through the lush indoor setting.

Is Center Parcs Elveden Forest good for babies?

Yes, it's fantastic for babies. There are baby changing stations, baby sensory classes, shallow pool areas, Ella's Kitchen baby food stations, and high chairs and cots in the lodges. It's a very family- and baby-friendly environment.

How much is Center Parcs for a week with a family?

Prices vary greatly depending on the season, size of your lodge, and how early you book. We visited during term time and saved significantly, but you can expect to pay more during school holidays. Check the prices shown during booking for the best deals, and consider that Center Parcs does offer discounts for repeat visitors.

Are restaurants at Center Parcs Elveden family-friendly?

Absolutely. We especially enjoyed Las Iguanas for both the food and family-friendly service. They even had a robot waiter, which the kids loved. Other options include Huck's, the Pancake House, Bella Italia, and more — though it's wise to book early.
item.excerpt:encoded: Planning your first holiday with a baby? Wondering whether Center Parcs Elveden Forest is worth it for families with young children? Here's our honest, in-depth review based on our first family holiday with a 7-month-old and three older girls (ages 6–10) — and why we now recommend Center Parcs over caravan parks like Parkdean.

We took our baby and three girls to Center Parcs Elveden Forest — here’s our honest 2025 review of the pool, lodges, activities, food and more.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: We visited this Centerparc for the first time this May. In fact it was our first Centerparc visit ever. I am adverse to anything remotely like a holiday village (Hi Di Hi). We went with our daughter, son in law and 2 grandsons aged 3 and 5 months. It was far better than I could have imagined. Seeing the excitement on the 3yo's face when the geese, squirrels, deer came up onto our patio was something not to be missed. Being able to cook our own meals in the well appointed kitchen was a blessing with those of us with dietary issues. I loved the electric boat ride as we were able to get up close to the various wildfowl on the lake and point out where the birds were nesting to the grandson etc. Grandson took part in the science workshop and was fully engaged whereas the Balance Bike workshop was a miserable flop for him. He also did the Nature Walk and came back full of the things he had seen and collected. It also gave him a book to put all the things in and record what he had seen and done. A great hit with his Nursery school. We saved the Pancake House until day of departure - a wise move but it was rather noisy for my taste. The playpark and the Pool complex were a highlight. The Aqua Sana Spa experience was really good for our stressed and exhausted daughter and son in law as it gave them a bit of time to unwind and I have urged them to book it for when we go again next year. I will also encourage them to have an evening meal out while we babysit. Yes, I am a convert to Centerparcs for overburdened families. They have so much to contend with. We go in January so looking forward to the Winter Lights but maybe not so much in the way of wildlife - who knows.
Hi there, I enjoy reading all of your article post. I like to write a little comment to support you.
thanks, I enjoyed the read - what is the forest craft kit you mention?!

item.title: Child Maintenance Service (CMS) Changes 2025: What UK Parents Need to Know
item.dc:creator: danieljbetts89@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
If you're a separated parent in the UK, there are significant CMS changes coming to the Child Maintenance Service...and they could affect how much child maintenance you pay or receive, how quickly payments are enforced, and what financial support you get.

The government has announced on 23rd June that a new set of reforms that aim to improve how child maintenance is managed, enforced, and transferred.

Here's everything you need to know in plain English, including when the changes will take place and what they mean for families like yours.

Note: Where statistics are referenced, they are mostly pulled from the Government Consultation outcome document referenced above, unless otherwise stated.

When Do the CMS Changes Start?

OK, so there's good news and bad news.

We'll start with the bad news: The CMS referred to in this article won't come into force until 2027 at the earliest as they require new legislation and system updates.

I've spoken to hundreds, if not thousands of separated parents over the years and I know reform can't come soon enough for so many people.

So unfortunately, before we go any further, I thought it'd be grounding the article in reality. For now at least, whether you're using Direct Pay or the Collect and Pay service, the same process will remain in place.

Why Are These CMS Changes Happening?

As I mentioned above, it's clear that the Child Maintenance Service is not without its issues.

In fact, the statistics paint a clear picture:

  • Only 60% of Direct Pay users receive the full child maintenance they’re owed from the other parent
  • Just 40% get payments on time

With over 750,000 families using the CMS, these failures in the child maintenance arrangement have had, and continue to have, a real impact on the lives of children.

What Are the Main CMS Changes?

1. Faster Enforcement After Missed Payments

CMS will now be able to take action after just one missed payment, helping reduce arrears and make enforcement more effective from day one.

2. Automatic Deductions from Bank Accounts

CMS will gain the power to automatically deduct payments from a paying parent’s bank account, without requiring a court order.

3. A New Service Structure

Direct Pay and Collect and Pay will merge into a single monitored service, offering improved consistency and oversight across all cases.

4. New Fees for Everyone

A 2% fee will be applied to both paying and receiving parents, even those who previously used fee-free Direct Pay:

  • Paying parent: pays 102%
  • Receiving parent: receives 98%

The 20% surcharge for enforcement remains.

Direct Pay Changes and What They Mean for Families

Direct Pay users will now face fees for the first time. This will impact families who previously chose this option to avoid charges. While the government argues the fees fund better enforcement, many parents will need to factor this into future budgets.

How CMS Changes Affect Paying Parents

Paying parents will see:

  • Enforcement after one missed payment
  • No need for court orders to deduct payments
  • A 2% service charge
  • Increased monitoring and accountability

Collect and Pay Service Transformation

The new system will replace the existing Collect and Pay option, bringing:

  • Fewer service distinctions
  • Consistent enforcement rules
  • Professional oversight
  • The 2% fee (replacing Collect and Pay’s previous fees)

CMS Support for Domestic Abuse Survivors

Previously, survivors could avoid Collect and Pay to reduce contact. These new reforms may limit that flexibility.

The government has promised safeguards for vulnerable parents who have experienced domestic abuse, and organisations like Gingerbread are calling for trauma-informed processes.

If you're navigating child maintenance after domestic abuse, you may find my guide to parallel parenting helpful.

Family-Based Arrangements and the Transition to CMS

Private arrangements will still be possible, but the CMS will encourage more families to transition to the official system. The new structure promises better enforcement, but also introduces fees, so families should weigh up whether professional oversight is worth the cost.

CMS Changes in Northern Ireland

Northern Ireland runs its own CMS, but it often aligns with UK-wide changes. Parents should monitor updates from NI Direct for confirmation of how reforms may be mirrored locally.

Addressing Child Poverty Through Better Enforcement

Irregular child maintenance contributes to child poverty. The government hopes better enforcement will lead to more consistent payments, easing pressure on single-parent households.
(Source: Parliament Briefing)

Will the CMS Recalculate Maintenance Payments?

Yes, a future consultation will review how maintenance is calculated, which could impact:

  • Self-employed parents
  • Families receiving benefits
  • Parents with irregular incomes

(Source: The Independent)

What Campaigners Are Calling For

Charities like Gingerbread are asking for:

  • A child poverty-first approach
  • Clearer communication and updates
  • Post-enforcement support
  • Adequate CMS staffing and digital systems
  • Greater transparency and accountability

Key Proposals Summary

  • 2027 implementation – no changes yet
  • One missed payment triggers enforcement
  • Unified service replaces Direct Pay and Collect and Pay
  • 2% fees apply to all
  • Bank deductions without court involvement
  • Calculation review planned for later stages
  • Domestic abuse protections still being developed

Final Thoughts

Child maintenance isn’t a bonus, it’s a basic need. These reforms could mark a real shift in how the CMS supports parents and children across the UK.

For many, it means more predictable support. For others, the changes bring new costs and concerns. Either way, knowing what’s coming helps you prepare.

Need help navigating child maintenance or co-parenting? Visit my Separated Parents section for guides, insights, and resources. And if you want to stay organised, check out the best co-parenting apps in the UK.

Frequently Asked Questions

When do the CMS changes take effect?

The changes to the Child Maintenance Service are expected to come into force in 2027 at the earliest, following new legislation and a system rollout.

Will I have to pay fees if I use Direct Pay for CMS?

Yes, under the new CMS system, all parents—whether using Direct Pay or not—will be charged a 2% fee on payments.

What happens if a parent misses a CMS payment?

The CMS will be able to take enforcement action after just one missed payment, including direct deductions from bank accounts.

Can I still make a private child maintenance arrangement?

Family-based arrangements will still be possible, but the new CMS structure encourages monitored payments with improved enforcement.

Will the way child maintenance is calculated change?

Yes, the government plans to consult on how maintenance is calculated in a future stage of reform, which may affect self-employed and variable-income parents.
item.excerpt:encoded: Child maintenance is changing. From new enforcement rules to a 2% fee for all users, here’s what separated parents in the UK need to know about the CMS reforms coming in 2025 and beyond.
